faqs.question: How do I get to Rasdhoo Island from Male?
faqs.answer: You can reach Rasdhoo Island from Male by public ferry or speedboat. The public ferry operates three times a week (Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday), departing from Male at 9:00 AM and arriving at Rasdhoo around 12:30 PM. Some guesthouses also offer private transfers for a higher fee. For early morning hammerhead shark dives, it's recommended to arrive the day before.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Rasdhoo Island?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit Rasdhoo Island depends on your priorities. January to March offers the highest chance of hammerhead sightings. The northeast monsoon (December-April) generally provides the best overall weather conditions with less rainfall and lower humidity. The southwest monsoon (May-November) may have occasional rain showers but still offers many sunny days, fewer tourists, and better chances to see manta rays due to higher plankton levels. Water temperature remains warm (27-30°C/80-86°F) year-round.

faqs.question: Do I need to be a certified diver to dive in Rasdhoo?
faqs.answer: While many of Rasdhoo's famous dive sites like Hammerhead Point require advanced certification due to depth and currents, there are options for divers of all levels. Beginners can take a Discover Scuba Diving course to experience diving under close supervision in shallow, calm waters. The house reef and some nearby sites are suitable for novice divers. For those wanting to get certified, all dive centers on Rasdhoo offer PADI and/or SSI certification courses from Open Water to advanced levels. Non-divers can still enjoy Rasdhoo's marine life through snorkeling trips to the house reef and nearby coral gardens.

faqs.question: Are there any dress code requirements on Rasdhoo Island?
faqs.answer: Yes, as Rasdhoo is a local inhabited island with a Muslim population, visitors are expected to dress modestly in public areas. Both men and women should cover shoulders and knees when walking around the village, visiting shops, or dining in local restaurants. Swimwear (including bikinis) is only permitted at the designated "bikini beach" area on the eastern side of the island. When visiting the mosque or religious sites, women should cover their heads with a scarf. These dress code requirements are a sign of respect for local culture and traditions and are generally well-enforced on the island.

faqs.question: What facilities are available for non-divers on Rasdhoo?
faqs.answer: While Rasdhoo is famous for diving, non-divers will find plenty to enjoy. The island offers excellent snorkeling directly from the beach, with equipment available for rent from guesthouses and dive centers. Water sports like kayaking, stand-up paddleboarding, and jet skiing are available. Cultural experiences include village tours, cooking classes, and traditional Boduberu performances. Excursions to nearby uninhabited islands, sandbanks, and resort day trips are popular. The bikini beach is perfect for swimming and sunbathing. Rasdhoo also has several cafés, restaurants, and shops to explore, plus opportunities to interact with the friendly local community.
